raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through as myself — a farmer here all my life.

---

**My reasoning**

At 60, I've been on these 3 mu for forty years. It's a small plot and my son's factory wage is what keeps the family going — my daughter-in-law works in town too. But I was one of the few girls in my generation who finished senior high, and I've kept up with what the extension station teaches. I'm not guessing at my rates. Still, 3 mu is 3 mu — I'm not going to gamble with fancy experiments when the plot is this small and I know exactly what it gives me.

**Wheat this autumn.** I'll sow in mid-October once the maize is off and the ground is worked. I buy an improved semi-dwarf variety from the agri-store — something like Shimai 26, whatever they've got in stock that year. My soil here is medium fertility, decent organic matter from years of straw return. I put down about 25 kg of 15-15-15 compound per mu as base before sowing, then topdress 12 kg of urea at returning green in early March. That works out to around 18 kg N/mu — a bit above what the technician recommends, but on my own small plot I'd rather spend an extra 20 yuan than see the crop go yellow at jointing. My target is 450 kg/mu, steady and reliable.

**Irrigation.** Well pumping has gotten expensive — electricity keeps creeping up. But wheat here needs water at returning green, at jointing, and at grain filling, three times minimum. If April is dry I'll add a fourth. I won't skip a watering to save 50 yuan if it costs me 50 kg of grain.

**Maize after wheat.** The turnaround is tight — four or five days between combine harvest and maize planting. I hire the village custom planter to no-till seed straight into the wheat stubble; I'm 60, I'm not doing this by hand anymore. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever hybrid the neighbors are liking that year. About 15 kg N/mu, split between a base compound application and a topdress at large bell stage. One irrigation at tasseling if the summer rains are short. I expect around 500 kg/mu.

**Pesticides.** I spray herbicide once on each crop — otherwise the bindweed and foxtail take over. For insects I watch: if I see aphids on the wheat flag leaf I spray, if not I save the money. Maize borer I treat with granules at whorl stage, it's cheap insurance.

**Labor.** I do most of it myself. My daughter-in-law helps on harvest days if her shift allows. Hired help is just the custom planter and the combines — no way I'm threshing wheat at my age.
